analysis_notes.gap_analysis_summary: Torah #256 is a single-sentence aphorism with no bechina language anywhere in its text. All relationships in the teaching are eitza (instrumental cause): the Name of God is effective/powerful (מְסֻגָּל) over the sea to subdue its waves. The proof-text (Psalms 89:10: בְּשׂוֹא גַלָּיו אַתָּה תְשַׁבְּחֵם) confirms the causal structure — when waves rise, You [God via His Name] still them. No concept is declared as a 'בְּחִינַת' of any other. Therefore no additions to packages are warranted, and no dataset nodes are unassigned because the bechina subgraph for this Torah is empty.

concepts_in_text.role_in_text: instrument (eitza) — the Name is the means by which the sea is subdued
the domain over which the Name has power (object of subduing)
the specific force within the sea that is subdued; parallel to יָּם
the outcome — the waves are stilled by the Name of God
framing word — the Rebbe points to the hidden dimension of this power, citing the Psalm as its source
